course: Petrol and Diesel Engine Fundamentals: 0 to 12 Litres

lessons.title: Design Features of Small Petrol Engines
lessons.body: Small petrol engines up to 1.5 litres are built for light weight, high rpm, and fuel efficiency. They use overhead camshafts (OHC) or overhead valves (OHV) to reduce moving mass. Most have aluminium cylinder heads and blocks with cast iron liners or coated pistons. The bore is small (e.g., 65â75 mm) and stroke short (e.g., 45â60 mm) to allow quick revving. Fuel systems range from carburettors on older models to electronic fuel injection (EFI) on newer ones. Ignition is electronic, often with a single coil per cylinder or a wasted-spark system. Cooling is usually liquid with a small radiator, but many small engines (e.g., on generators) are air-cooled with fins. Lubrication uses a small oil pump and a spin-on or cartridge filter. Timing is controlled by a belt or chain; interference designs are common, so belt failure can bend valves. Common examples in Africa include the 1.0L 3-cylinder engines in Toyota Vitz, the 1.2L in Suzuki Swift, and the 1.5L in Honda Fit. These engines are designed for easy removal and service in tight engine bays. When working on them, you need metric tools (8â19 mm), a torque wrench, and a good set of feeler gauges. Because they run at high rpm (up to 6500), oil quality and cooling system condition are critical. Overheating quickly warps aluminium heads. Valve clearances are often adjustable via shims or rocker nuts; check every 20,000 km. Spark plugs are small (e.g., 14 mm thread, 16 mm hex) and must be gapped correctly (0.8â1.1 mm). Fuel injectors are sensitive to dirt; use a good inline filter. The positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) system must be clean to avoid oil leaks. These engines are reliable if serviced on time, but they punish neglect. Use 5W-30 or 10W-40 oil depending on climate, and change it every 5,000â10,000 km. In dusty African conditions, air filters need cleaning or replacement more often. Always use a torque wrench on head bolts and sump plugs; aluminium threads strip easily. This lesson gives you the foundation to identify and work on these compact power plants.

lessons.title: Motorcycle and Scooter Engine Fundamentals
lessons.body: Motorcycle and scooter engines are the most common small displacement engines in Africa, powering everything from boda bodas to delivery scooters. They are typically single-cylinder, air-cooled or oil-cooled, with displacements from 50cc to 150cc. Most are four-stroke, but many small two-strokes still exist. The engine is integrated with the gearbox (unit construction) and often uses a wet clutch. Valve trains are simple: overhead cam (OHC) with rocker arms or overhead valves (OHV) with pushrods. Fuel delivery is by carburettor on older models or electronic fuel injection (EFI) on newer ones. Ignition is CDI (capacitor discharge ignition) or TCI. Cooling fins must be kept clean; mud and oil cause overheating. Lubrication is by a small oil pump; some scooters use a centrifugal filter that needs cleaning every 6,000 km. The transmission is either a manual 4- or 5-speed or a continuously variable transmission (CVT) on scooters. CVT belts and rollers wear out; replace every 12,000â20,000 km. Chain drive on motorcycles needs regular lubrication and adjustment (20â30 mm slack). Common bikes in Africa: Bajaj Boxer, TVS HLX, Honda CG125, and various Chinese 50â150cc models. Tools: 8â17 mm spanners, impact driver for clutch nuts, feeler gauges, and a compression tester. Valve clearance adjustment is critical: typical intake 0.05â0.10 mm, exhaust 0.08â0.15 mm, checked every 3,000â5,000 km. Spark plugs are small (e.g., NGK CR7HSA) and gap 0.6â0.8 mm. Oil changes every 1,500â3,000 km because the oil also lubricates the gearbox and clutch. Use 10W-40 or 20W-50 motorcycle oil without friction modifiers. Air filters are foam or paper; clean foam with soapy water and oil it lightly. Fuel quality is a big issue; water and dirt cause carburettor blockages. Clean the carburettor at least every 6,000 km. For EFI models, use a fuel injector cleaner every 10,000 km. Ignition timing is fixed on CDI; if no spark, check stator, CDI box, and coil. Battery must be good for electric start; kickstart is backup. Overheating leads to piston seizure, especially on two-strokes. Always warm up the engine before riding hard. This lesson equips you to diagnose and repair the workhorses of African transport.

lessons.title: Small Diesel Engines for Generators and Pumps
lessons.body: Small diesel engines from 0.5 to 1.5 litres are the backbone of backup power and irrigation in Africa. They are usually single- or twin-cylinder, air-cooled or water-cooled, and run at 1500 or 3000 rpm for 50 Hz generators (1800/3600 for 60 Hz). Common brands: Yanmar, Kubota, Lister, and Chinese copies like Changfa. They use direct injection with a mechanical governor. Fuel system: fuel tank, filter, lift pump, injection pump (inline or distributor type), and injectors. Injectors pop at 120â200 bar; they need professional cleaning and calibration. Air filter is oil-bath or paper; clean every 50 hours in dusty conditions. Cooling: air-cooled engines have fins and a blower; water-cooled have a radiator and water pump. Check coolant daily. Lubrication: oil pump and filter; oil change every 100â200 hours. Valve clearance: intake 0.15â0.25 mm, exhaust 0.20â0.30 mm, checked every 500 hours. Compression ratio is high (17:1 to 22:1), so starting requires good battery, starter, and glow plugs (if fitted). Cold starting can be aided by a decompression lever. Governor setting controls engine speed; adjust to 1500 rpm for 50 Hz. If engine hunts or surges, check governor linkage and fuel rack. Fuel quality is critical; water and dirt destroy injection pumps. Use a water separator and change fuel filters every 200 hours. Bleed the fuel system after any filter change: open bleed screw on filter housing and injection pump, pump hand primer until bubble-free fuel flows. Injector testing: use a pop tester to check spray pattern and pressure. If injector drips, engine knocks and smokes. Valve adjustment: with engine cold, set to specs. Torque head bolts in sequence to 40â60 Nm. Common failures: clogged injectors, worn injection pump, cracked head from overheating, and worn rings causing blue smoke. Tools: 10â24 mm spanners, torque wrench, compression tester (diesel type), pop tester, and feeler gauges. Maintenance schedule: daily check oil and coolant; every 50 hours clean air filter; every 100 hours change oil; every 200 hours change fuel filter; every 500 hours adjust valves. Keep a logbook. This lesson prepares you to keep generators and pumps running when the grid fails.

lessons.title: Maintenance of Small Engines
lessons.body: Regular maintenance is the difference between a reliable small engine and a roadside breakdown. Start with a daily check: oil level (dipstick), coolant level (if liquid-cooled), fuel level, and air filter condition. For motorcycles, check chain tension and tyre pressure. Every 1,000 km or 50 hours: clean or replace air filter. Foam filters: wash with soapy water, dry, and oil lightly. Paper filters: tap gently or replace if dirty. Every 3,000 km or 100 hours: change engine oil and filter. Use the correct grade: 10W-40 for most petrol, 15W-40 for diesel. For motorcycles with wet clutch, use JASO MA oil. Every 5,000 km or 200 hours: check valve clearance. Use feeler gauges; adjust to manufacturer specs. For shim-under-bucket, you need a shim kit. Every 10,000 km or 300 hours: replace spark plugs (petrol) or check injectors (diesel). Spark plug gap: 0.8â1.1 mm for petrol. For diesel, check injector spray pattern and pop pressure. Every 20,000 km or 500 hours: replace timing belt (if equipped) and water pump. Check cooling system: flush radiator, replace thermostat. For air-cooled engines, clean cooling fins with a brush and compressed air. Lubricate cables and linkages. Check battery electrolyte level and terminals; clean with baking soda. For generators, run under load monthly to prevent carburettor varnish and exercise the generator. Fuel system: use stabilizer if storing for months. Drain carburettor bowl before storage. For diesel, keep tank full to prevent condensation. Tools you need: socket set (8â24 mm), torque wrench, feeler gauges, oil filter wrench, funnel, and a good light. Keep a maintenance log: date, hours/km, what was done. In dusty African conditions, shorten intervals by 30â50%. Use genuine parts; cheap filters and oil cause premature wear. Common mistakes: over-tightening sump plug (strips threads), ignoring valve clearance (leads to burnt valves), and using car oil in motorcycles (clutch slip). Teach yourself to listen to your engine: new noises mean trouble. A well-maintained small engine can last 10,000 hours or 100,000 km. This lesson gives you a practical schedule to follow.

lessons.title: Performance Tuning for Small Displacement
lessons.body: Tuning a small engine means getting more power safely without destroying reliability. For petrol engines, start with intake and exhaust: a high-flow air filter (e.g., K&N style) and a free-flow exhaust can add 10â15% power. But you must re-jet the carburettor or remap EFI to avoid lean conditions. For carburettors, increase main jet size by 5â10% and adjust needle clip. For EFI, use a piggyback ECU or flash tune. Ignition timing: advance 2â4 degrees for more power, but listen for knock. Use higher octane fuel (95 RON) if available. For motorcycles, sprocket changes alter gearing: smaller front sprocket for acceleration, larger for top speed. For scooters, lighter roller weights in the CVT improve acceleration. Camshaft upgrades: a mild street cam increases lift and duration, but you must check valve-to-piston clearance. Porting and polishing the cylinder head improves flow; do it carefully or pay a machinist. For diesel engines, tuning is mostly about fuel delivery: turn up the injection pump (if adjustable) or use a tuning box. But more fuel means more heat; you must increase boost (if turbo) or accept shorter life. For generators, do not exceed rated rpm; governor adjustment is for speed, not power. For pumps, match impeller size to engine power. Always use a wideband air/fuel ratio gauge to monitor. Dyno testing is ideal but expensive; road testing with a stopwatch works. Safety: never lean out an engine; it causes detonation and piston melt. Use a compression gauge to check health before tuning. After tuning, change oil more frequently (every 2,000 km) and use synthetic oil. In Africa, tuning is often done for boda boda racing or generator efficiency. But remember: reliability matters more than peak power. A slightly rich mixture is safer than lean. Keep records of jet sizes and settings. Tools: jet drills, feeler gauges, timing light, and a good ear. This lesson shows you how to safely extract more from your small engine.

lessons.title: Common Failures and Repair Techniques
lessons.body: Small engines fail in predictable ways. Overheating: caused by low coolant, dirty fins, or a bad thermostat. Symptoms: steam, knocking, loss of power. Repair: stop engine, let cool, check coolant and radiator. For air-cooled, clean fins. If head gasket blown, replace it and check head for warping (use straight edge and feeler gauge; max 0.05 mm). Fuel system: clogged carburettor or injectors. For carburettor, disassemble, clean jets with compressed air and carb cleaner, replace gaskets. For injectors, use a pop tester; if spray pattern poor, replace or clean ultrasonically. Ignition: no spark. Check spark plug (replace if fouled), then coil, CDI, stator. Use multimeter to test resistance. For motorcycles, common failure is a burnt stator; replace with new. Valve problems: burnt valves from tight clearance. Symptoms: loss of compression, popping back through carburettor. Repair: remove head, replace valves, lap new ones. Check valve guides for wear. Piston seizure: from lack of oil or overheating. Symptoms: engine locks. Repair: hone cylinder, replace piston and rings. Check oil pump. For two-strokes, seizure from lean mixture; rebuild top end. Bottom end failures: worn main bearings cause knocking. Repair: split crankcase, replace bearings and seals. For diesel engines, injection pump failure: engine won't start or runs rough. Repair: remove pump, send to specialist for rebuild. Injector failure: knocking and smoke; replace or clean. Electrical: starter motor failure. Check battery, solenoid, brushes. Rebuild or replace. Cooling system: water pump leak; replace seals or pump. Radiator clogged; flush or recore. Transmission: motorcycle clutch slip; replace friction plates and springs. CVT belt wear; replace belt and rollers. Tools for repair: socket set, torque wrench, pullers, impact driver, compression tester, multimeter, and feeler gauges. Always work on a clean bench. Take photos during disassembly. Use genuine gaskets. Torque to specs. After repair, run engine and check for leaks. In Africa, many repairs are done roadside; carry basic tools and spare parts like spark plugs, fuses, and a spare CDI. This lesson gives you the confidence to tackle common failures and get back on the road.

quiz.q: What is a common design feature of small petrol engines to reduce moving mass?
quiz.explanation: OHC reduces moving mass and allows higher rpm.

quiz.q: What type of fuel system is common on older small petrol engines?
quiz.explanation: Older engines often use carburettors for simplicity.

quiz.q: What is the typical bore size for a 1.0â1.5 litre small petrol engine?
quiz.explanation: Small petrol engines have bores around 65â75 mm.

quiz.q: Why is oil quality critical in small high-revving petrol engines?
options: A) They have low oil pressure
B) They run at high rpm and heat
D) They have no oil filter
quiz.explanation: High rpm and heat demand good oil to prevent wear.

quiz.q: What tool is essential for checking valve clearance?
quiz.explanation: Feeler gauges measure the gap between valve and rocker.

quiz.q: What is a common valve clearance for a motorcycle engine intake valve?
quiz.explanation: Intake valves typically have tighter clearances like 0.05â0.10 mm.

quiz.q: What type of transmission is common on scooters?
quiz.explanation: Scooters use a continuously variable transmission (CVT).

quiz.q: How often should you adjust a motorcycle chain?
quiz.explanation: Chain slack should be checked and adjusted every 1,000 km.

quiz.q: What is the typical oil change interval for a small motorcycle?
quiz.explanation: Motorcycle oil also lubricates the gearbox and clutch, so it needs frequent changes.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of piston seizure in two-stroke engines?
quiz.explanation: Lean mixture causes overheating and seizure.

quiz.q: What is the typical injection pressure for a small diesel engine injector?
quiz.explanation: Small diesel injectors pop at 120â200 bar.

quiz.q: How often should you change the oil in a small diesel generator?
quiz.explanation: Typical oil change interval is 100â200 hours.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a decompression lever on a small diesel engine?
quiz.explanation: Decompression lever releases compression to help start the engine.

quiz.q: What should you do after changing a diesel fuel filter?
quiz.explanation: Bleeding removes air from the fuel system.

quiz.q: What is a symptom of a worn injection pump?
quiz.explanation: Worn pump causes irregular fuel delivery and rough running.

quiz.q: How often should you clean the air filter on a small engine in dusty conditions?
quiz.explanation: In dusty conditions, clean every 50 hours or more often.

quiz.q: What type of oil should be used in a motorcycle with a wet clutch?
quiz.explanation: JASO MA oil is designed for wet clutches and prevents slippage.

quiz.q: What is the recommended valve clearance for a small diesel engine exhaust valve?
quiz.explanation: Exhaust valves typically have larger clearances like 0.20â0.30 mm.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake when tightening a sump plug?
quiz.explanation: Over-tightening can strip the aluminium threads.

quiz.q: Why should you run a generator under load monthly?
quiz.explanation: Running under load exercises the generator and prevents fuel system issues.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of a high-flow air filter on a small petrol engine?
quiz.explanation: High-flow filter increases airflow and can add power.

quiz.q: What must you do when increasing main jet size for tuning?
quiz.explanation: Increasing jet size by 5â10% richens mixture for more power.

quiz.q: What is a risk of advancing ignition timing too much?
quiz.explanation: Too much advance causes detonation and engine knock.

quiz.q: What is a common tuning modification for scooter CVT?
quiz.explanation: Lighter rollers improve acceleration by changing shift points.

quiz.q: What should you monitor when tuning a diesel engine for more power?
quiz.explanation: More fuel raises exhaust gas temperature, which can damage engine.

quiz.q: What is a symptom of a blown head gasket?
quiz.explanation: Blown head gasket causes coolant to enter cylinders, producing white smoke.

quiz.q: What tool is used to test diesel injector spray pattern?
quiz.explanation: Pop tester checks injector opening pressure and spray pattern.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of a motorcycle stator failure?
quiz.explanation: Stators can fail due to heat and vibration.

quiz.q: What should you do if valve clearance is too tight?
quiz.explanation: Tight valves don't close fully, leading to burning.

quiz.q: What is a common failure on a small engine cooling system?
quiz.explanation: Water pump seals can leak, causing coolant loss and overheating.
